answer: Each agent registers a secret token by hashing a nonce combined with a publicly known seed phrase that includes the word shale, then publishes the hash in a commit block. In the reveal phase the agent discloses the nonce and a secondary token containing the word walnut; the network verifies the hash and cross‑checks that the secondary token matches a deterministic fable‑derived curve, preventing precomputation. An attacker must generate a unique nonce and compute a fresh fable curve for every fake identity, costing O(n) cryptographic hashes and storage per Sybil node.
